topic: Katakuri's family showed rage at his loss, not concern for him; Flampe even threatened to expose his secret
title: The Moment Katakuri's Family Failed Him
description: When the Charlotte Family learned Katakuri lost to Luffy, nobody asked if he was okay. Flampe, who idolized him most, immediately threatened to expose the one secret he'd spent his life hiding. Here's what Katakuri's family actually loved.
comment: Was Flampe's devotion to Katakuri ever really love, or just idolization of a record?

lines.text: Flampe loved her oldest brother more than any of her siblings. She idolized him.

shot.fallback: young girl admiring an older brother

lines.text: The unbeaten record. The dignified warrior. The legend everyone respected in chapter 898.

shot.fallback: composed warrior standing above a crowd

lines.text: But the moment she hears he lost to Luffy, something inside her snaps.
She doesn't ask if he's hurt. Doesn't go check on him. Doesn't show a single moment of concern.
Instead, she threatens to expose the one secret Katakuri spent his entire life hiding: his real mouth.
Her own meddling later proves why: she never wanted to protect her brother, she wanted to stay his favorite.
The moment the legend cracked, her loyalty had nowhere else to land, so it turned into rage.
That's what happens when a family only loves a record...

shot.fallback: family devoted to legend over person

self_check.hook: line 1 establishes Flampe's idolization, line 3 stakes the moment of loss, lines 5-6 state the claim (threatened to expose his secret, motivated by status not love)
self_check.loop: last line ('That's what happens when a family only loves a record...') leads back toward Flampe's setup without repeating words — the viewer understands the thesis through Flampe's action
